name: Abia
overview: The name Abia, also known as Abijah, appears in Scripture primarily as the son of Samuel who, along with his brother Joel, served as a judge in Beersheba but failed to follow their father's righteous example, instead turning to corrupt practices. Additionally, Abia is recognized as the chief of the twenty-four courses of priests, highlighting his leadership role in Israel's worship. The biblical record also identifies Abia as a king of Judah, reflecting the name's association with significant spiritual and political leadership within God's people.
